hook.line: Sooner or later someone asks you something you truly cannot answer. Spanish has a friendly, slightly stronger way to say so than a plain "I don't know".
hook.es: No tengo ni idea de dónde están las llaves.
hook.en: I have no idea where the keys are.

examples.es: No tengo ni idea de qué hacer.
examples.en: I have no idea what to do.

examples.es: No tengo ni idea de dónde están las llaves.
examples.en: I have no idea where the keys are.

examples.es: No tienes ni idea de cuántos años tiene don Hernando.
examples.en: You have no idea how old don Hernando is (to a friend).

examples.es: No tenía ni idea de que estuvieras en Bogotá.
examples.en: I had no idea you were in Bogotá.

rule:
*No tengo ni idea de* is "I have no idea" with a little extra push: *ni* means not even. After *de*, put a question word (*qué*, *dónde*, *quién*, *cuánto*) or a noun.

*No tengo ni idea de qué hacer.*

It bends like *tener*: *no tienes ni idea*, *no tiene ni idea*, *no teníamos ni idea*.

For something you did not know was true, use *de que*. In the past, the next verb is usually in the "-ra" form: *No tenía ni idea de que estuvieras aquí.* Among friends, a bare *Ni idea* is a complete answer.
smallPrint: Teachers call *ni idea* an emphatic negative expression of ignorance (*expresión de desconocimiento*).

readAndPick.es: No tengo ni idea de qué hacer.
options: I have no idea what to do.
I have an idea of what to do.
I did not know what to do.
I have no idea.
I have an idea.

readAndPick.es: No tienes ni idea de cuántos años tiene don Hernando.
options: I have no idea how old don Hernando is.
You have no idea how old don Hernando is.

readAndPick.es: No tenía ni idea de que estuvieras aquí.
options: I have no idea you are here.
I had no idea you were here.
I will have no idea you are here.

readAndPick.es: No tenemos ni idea de dónde está.
options: We have no idea where it is.
They have no idea where it is.
I have no idea where it is.

readAndPick.es: No tienen ni idea de quién es.
options: He has no idea who it is.
They have no idea who it is.
You have no idea who it is (to a friend).
No idea.
I have an idea.
What an idea.

readAndPick.es: No teníamos ni idea de dónde estaba.
options: We have no idea where he is.
We had no idea where he was.
We will have no idea where he is.

options: She has no idea how to cook.
She has no idea what is cooking.
They have no idea how to cook.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tengo* or *tienes*, and type the whole sentence: I have no idea what to do.
yourTurn.answer: No tengo ni idea de qué hacer.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I have no idea where the keys are.
yourTurn.answer: No tengo ni idea de dónde están las llaves.
yourTurn.why: After *de* comes the question word, then the clause.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: You have no idea how old don Hernando is.
yourTurn.answer: No tienes ni idea de cuántos años tiene don Hernando.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We have no idea who it is.
yourTurn.answer: No tenemos ni idea de quién es.
accept: No tenemos ni idea de quién es él.

yourTurn.prompt: Put it in the past: *No tenemos ni idea de dónde está.* (We had no idea where it was.)
yourTurn.answer: No teníamos ni idea de dónde estaba.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: They have no idea how to cook.
yourTurn.answer: No tienen ni idea de cocinar.
yourTurn.why: With a verb after *de*, use the plain infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type the quick friend answer to *¿Quién llamó?*: No idea.
yourTurn.why: Among friends, *ni idea* alone is enough.

pitfalls.right: No tengo ni idea de qué hacer.
pitfalls.why: The little word *de* links the idea to what comes after.

pitfalls.wrong: Tengo ni idea de qué hacer.
pitfalls.right: No tengo ni idea de qué hacer.
pitfalls.why: Spanish needs *no* before the verb as well as *ni*: two negatives, one meaning.

pitfalls.wrong: No tenía ni idea de que estás aquí.
pitfalls.right: No tenía ni idea de que estuvieras aquí.
pitfalls.why: After *no tenía ni idea de que*, Spanish uses the "-ra" form for something you did not expect.

personal: Say one thing you honestly have no idea about, with *No tengo ni idea de…*.
